---
title: "13. Health Economics and Financing"
---

## Overview

This module introduces participants to the role of health economics and financing in supporting malaria policy and programme decisions. Participants explore how modelling and economic evidence can inform prioritisation, resource allocation, and investment decisions in resource-constrained settings.

::: {.callout-tip appearance="default"}
## Learning Objectives

By the end of this module, participants should be able to:

-   How can economic evidence support policy and programme decisions?

-   What information is needed to assess affordability, sustainability, and value for money?

-   How can modelling inform funding allocations and investment strategies?
:::

::: {.callout-note appearance="default"}
## Key Concepts

-   Cost-effectiveness and value for money

-   Resource allocation and prioritisation

-   Affordability and sustainability

-   Investment cases and advocacy

-   Economic interpretation of modelling outputs
:::

Part 1: Introduction to Health Economics (30 min)

-   Why economics matters in programme decision-making

-   Linking modelling to resource allocation

Part 2: Economic Evidence and Policy (45 min)

-   Cost-effectiveness and prioritisation

-   Funding constraints and trade-offs

Part 3: Practical Exercise (45–60 min)

-   Participants compare intervention options under different budget scenarios

-   Discuss implications for programme priorities

Part 4: Group Discussion (30 min)

-   Using economic evidence for advocacy and investment

-   Balancing impact, feasibility, and affordability

Part 5: Reflection and Wrap-Up (15 min)

-   Key lessons for financing and prioritisation decisions

### Practical Exercise

Exercise Title: Prioritising Under Budget Constraints

**Instructions:\
** Participants:

1.  Review intervention options and budget scenarios

2.  Compare trade-offs between impact, cost, and feasibility

3.  Recommend a prioritised strategy

4.  Prepare a short justification for policymakers or funders

Groups present and discuss their recommendations.

### Facilitator Guidance

-   Focus on practical interpretation rather than technical economic methods

-   Reinforce that economic evidence supports—not replaces—policy judgement

-   Encourage discussion on operational realities and funding constraints

-   Use relatable programme examples and investment cases
